objective: Exploratory search under a frozen contract: every chain with linear rules on rings A, B and C (independently), declared ring sizes and contact positions, and contact laws given by their linear parts (proposal parities or self-blind laws u_A + u_B with u in {x, y, x + y}, chosen independently at each contact), decided exactly by row sequences: how many keep both contacts persistent, how many of those compose at every lag from d + 1 on, and, if any, verify the smallest on the full state space.
status: Supported 2026-11-08 (exploratory): of 9,216,000 affine chains, 45,406 keep both contacts persistent and 2,376 of those compose at every lag from d + 1 on (380 at both contacts); 430 with the contacts two or three cells apart, the middle ring carrying c1's past (rules 150, 60, 102, 90, 170, 240); H1 (forced gaps) fails; the smallest constructions verified on full state spaces, and the smallest carrying chain's knot confirmed by the generic enumerator and knotlab check.
title: Searching affine chains for persistent composition
